_README: Section 7 of the master prompt forbids inventing benchmarks. This file is the ONLY
source of reference values the report may use. If a variable has no entry here, the
report renders 'Individualized assessment required' for it. Nothing is inferred.
Every entry needs: value(s), units, population it applies to, evidence_class, and source.
literature          - a peer-reviewed study or federation technical manual, with citation
coaching_convention - a widely taught coaching target, NOT an empirical distribution
athlete_baseline    - computed from this athlete's own session, filled at runtime
SHIPPED EMPTY ON PURPOSE. Populating this is a sports-science task, not a coding task.
Add entries only when you can name the source. An entry with source set to null is
rejected by the S9 verifier and will block report publication.

entries.note: Placeholder. Fill target/range and source, or delete. Until then Section 7 renders 'Individualized assessment required' for this variable.

_note: Formulas, not population targets. They produce ESTIMATES, and every number
derived from them is printed with the formula name and the word estimate.
Section p1 may not print a heart-rate boundary that is not derived here.

max_heart_rate.source: Tanaka H, Monahan KD, Seals DR. Age-predicted maximal heart rate revisited. Journal of the American College of Cardiology 2001;37(1):153-156.
max_heart_rate.label: Tanaka age-predicted maximum (estimate)
max_heart_rate.note: Preferred over 220 - age, which overestimates in the young and underestimates in older adults. Population formula: an individual value can differ by roughly 10 bpm either way.

zones_pct_hrmax.source: American College of Sports Medicine. ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th edition, intensity classification by percentage of maximal heart rate.

bmi.note: Printed as a plain computed number with its formula. No category label, no health or body-composition reading is attached to it.

youth_age_threshold_years.source: Lloyd RS, Oliver JL et al. National Strength and Conditioning Association position statement on long-term athletic development. Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 2016;30(6):1491-1509.
youth_age_threshold_years.note: Below this age the plan states that volume, load progression and recovery follow youth guidelines and need coach sign-off. No load numbers are invented.
